answer:
NeurIPS 2026 style files **are published**.

- **Official ZIP:** https://media.neurips.cc/Conferences/NeurIPS2026/Formatting_Instructions_For_NeurIPS_2026.zip
- **Linked from official Call for Papers:** https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForPapers

The CFP lists the ZIP as the **“Paper template.”** The official NeurIPS 2026 CFP links directly to the paper-template ZIP. (https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForPapers)

I verified that the ZIP contains:

- `neurips_2026.sty`
- `neurips_2026.tex`
- `checklist.tex`

The style file identifies itself as `NeurIPS 2026 submission/camera-ready style file`. No ICML fallback is needed.

## Result

**Official source page:**  
https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForPapers

The 2026 main-conference CFP identifies itself as “The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)” and lists this under **Key links**:

> “Paper template”

linked to the archive below. Official NeurIPS 2026 CFP and its Paper template link.

**Exact official download URL:**  
https://media.neurips.cc/Conferences/NeurIPS2026/Formatting_Instructions_For_NeurIPS_2026.zip

The URL returns HTTP 200 as an `application/zip` file. Official NeurIPS media-domain ZIP download. (https://media.neurips.cc/Conferences/NeurIPS2026/Formatting_Instructions_For_NeurIPS_2026.zip)

### Archive inspection

The ZIP contains:

- `neurips_2026.tex`
- `checklist.tex`
- `neurips_2026.sty`

Exact evidence inside `neurips_2026.sty`:

```tex
% last revision: January 2026
\ProvidesPackage{neurips_2026}[2026-01-29 NeurIPS 2026 submission/camera-ready style file]
...
\newcommand{\@neuripsordinal}{40th}
\newcommand{\@neuripsyear}{2026}
```

Exact evidence inside `neurips_2026.tex`:

```tex
\title{Formatting Instructions For NeurIPS 2026}
```

```tex
The only supported style file for NeurIPS 2026 is
\verb+neurips_2026.sty+, rewritten for \LaTeXe{}.
```

## Assessment

**Yes, it is genuinely the 2026 style package.** It is linked directly by the official 2026 main-track CFP, hosted on the official `media.neurips.cc` domain, and internally identifies itself as the NeurIPS 2026 submission/camera-ready style.

There is no current `Styles.zip` filename: `/Conferences/2026/PaperInformation/StyleFiles` returns 404. The authoritative 2026 download is the `Formatting_Instructions_For_NeurIPS_2026.zip` archive above.

## Official source

**Linked-from page:**  
https://icml.cc/Conferences/2026/AuthorInstructions

The page states:

> “The required format of the papers is specified in the LaTeX style files…”

Its “LaTeX style files” link resolves directly to the ZIP below. “The required format of the papers is specified in the LaTeX style files and the example paper.”

The official Call for Papers independently links the same package:

https://icml.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForPapers

> “Please review Author Instructions, an Example Paper, and use the correct Style Files.” “Please review Author Instructions, an Example Paper, and use the correct Style Files.”

## Exact download URL

**Official style ZIP:**  
https://media.icml.cc/Conferences/ICML2026/Styles/icml2026.zip

Verified directly:

- HTTP status: `200`
- Content-Type: `application/zip`
- ZIP size: `228,368` bytes
- Valid ZIP signature: `PK`
- Contains nine files, including:
  - `icml2026.sty`, 27,344 bytes
  - `icml2026.bst`
  - `example_paper.tex`
  - `example_paper.pdf`

## Filename and year verification

Inside `icml2026.sty`:

```tex
% File: icml2026.sty (LaTeX style file for ICML-2026, version of 2025-10-29)
```

```tex
\ProvidesPackage{icml2026}[2025/10/29 v2.0 ICML Conference Style File]
```

Additional 2026-specific content:

```tex
Seoul, South Korea. PMLR 306, 2026.
Copyright 2026 by the author(s).
```

```tex
pdfsubject={Proceedings of the International Conference on Machine Learning 2026},
```

The bundled `example_paper.tex` also begins with:

```tex
%%%%%%%% ICML 2026 EXAMPLE LATEX SUBMISSION FILE %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
```

and loads:

```tex
\usepackage{icml2026}
```

**Conclusion:** The official package is unquestionably for **ICML 2026**. Its internal revision/package date is **2025-10-29**, which is the template’s release/version date, not a conference-year mismatch. The obvious standalone URL ending in `/icml2026.sty` returns `404`; the officially linked public download is the ZIP above.
